Question: What is your view on the death penalty?
Answer: I am against it. I want to preface this answer by saying that I believe that there are crimes that, if committed, forfeits the perpetuators life. That’s right, I believe that people do deserve to die if they commit a crime bad enough. However, I don’t believe that the government (this applies only to the United States) should execute people. Now, there are several reasons I believe this. Innocent people will get killed. This is a pretty indisputable fact. If you have the Death Penalty, eventually, innocent people will be executed. Since 1973, 185 prisoners have been taken off Death Row, according to the Death Penalty Information Center, with Florida releasing the most prisoners off death row.[1] We have examples of completely innocent people being killed, as well. Carlos DeLuna and Cameron Todd Willingham are both good examples of this. Timothy Evans was a rather famous case as well. And since 1992, 15 people have been found to be not guilty of any crime and released from Death Row.[2] Above: Timothy Evans In addition, we should note that no evidence is foolproof. Confessions can be coerced and forced. Video footage can be edited. Even forensic evidence can have been tampered with or improperly collected (or even faked altogether) which is a rather sobering thought. So yes, innocent people have and will continue to be executed. Cost This is a rather cold-hearted argument, but it’s true. Executing people, and the associated trials and appeals, cost more money then life imprisonment, with The Balance[3] noting It's more cost-effective to commute death penalties to life-imprisonment sentences without parole. There’s also not a lot we can do about the cost. Any attempts to shorten the appeal and trial process will inevitably lead to more innocent people getting executed, at which point the state is literally executing innocent people for money. And the Death Penalty doesn’t sound so fun when you put it that way. Racial Discrimination Our criminal justice system is messed up. I could write 5 answers on this, but I want to specifically note that black people and men get longer sentences for the same crime[4]. This means that inevitably, they will get executed more. The same applies to the race of the victim. A rather disturbing study found that if the victim of the crime in which the death penalty is sought, if the victim is white the death penalty is applied three times more frequently than if the victim was black and four times more frequently than if they were Latino. And of course, it shouldn’t surprise you that black prisoners are more likely to get the death sentence than white people for similar crimes[5]. Black people make up around ~14% of the population Other notes There are various issues with the Death Penalty I didn’t mention. For one, the methods of execution used can be frighteningly barbarian- even in modern times, hanging, firing squads, and gas chambers are used to execute people in the United States as well as the electric chair and lethal injection. Not to mention that people as young as 14 have been executed. George Stinny, a black kid, was accused of murdering two white girls. He was declared guilty by an all white jury summarily executed. However, it later came out that Stinny was innocent and had been forced to confess. Stinny would be in middle school at the time of his death Conclusion The Death Penalty is one of the oldest parts of our criminal justice system, and certainly one of the most archaic. It has been used to execute innocent people, and should be removed. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: What's the worst type of spice in Star Wars?
Answer: Engspice. (Trigger Warning: Drug Addiction) Basically, in Star Wars, spice is drugs. Engspice is sci-fi drugs taken to the extreme. In Star Wars, Engspice was a type of chemically altered spice that was incredibly addictive. It was bioengineered in such a way that taking it once would hook a user for life, or until they went through an agonizing and awful withdrawal process. Engspice, which was obviously illegal, was sold by criminal cartels like the Hutts and the Exchange. These enterprises made their own variants of Engspice, so that other sellers of engpsice didn’t steal their buyers- the Engspice addicts were addicted to one group’s spice alone, and no one elses. Engspice was also incredibly expensive. Users would find themselves selling everything they had to get more Engspice- eventually, turning to a life of crime and winding up in an Engspice Den. As it was such a lucrative market, many gang wars were fought over the Engspice market- if an addict couldn’t get one gang’s fix, the next best option was another’s. While this hasn’t been explicitly mentioned in Star Wars, the implications of such a nefarious drug extend past what we know in the lore. Criminal enterprises could theoretically alter Engspice into a minute and tasteless powder that they could sneak into people’s food- essentially, getting them hooked without that person’s consent to take drugs in the first place. Judging by the fact that there were quite a few Engspice users in the galaxy, it’s quite possible this was the case. Even if it wasn’t, however, Engspice remains one of the most brutal and awful secrets in the Star Wars universe. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: What is the best example of "lost the battle but won the war" in Star Wars?
Answer: The Battle of Kashyyyk. No, not that one. The one during the Second Galactic Civil War. See, following the battle of Gillater VIII, the Confederation- at war with the Galactic Alliance- began a major push to the core. This two pronged assault saw better trained Bothan and Commenorian units push towards the critical shipbuilding world of Kuat while the less disciplined Hutt and Commenorian forces attacked the factory world of Balmorra. Hutt forces begin their assault on Balmorra Darth Caedus, now commanding the Galactic Alliance, realized that if the Confederation took Kuat, they could strike at Coruscant, ending the war before the Galactic Alliance’s superior military industrial complex could turn the tide of the war. Caedus defeated the Hutts and Commenorians at Balmorra, before turning his attention to Kuat. Kuat would be the largest battle of the war. Indeed, thousands of capital ships and over 11,000 starfighters dueled and fought. Caedus understood that whoever would win Kuat would win the war. If the Confederation won, they would push on to Coruscant and end the war. If the Galactic Alliance won, they would secure the core long enough for the overwhelming size of their military industrial complex to react. Caedus was able to secure the allegiance of the Hapan Home Fleet, and with it he was able to gain an advantage at Kuat. Yet at the cusp of victory, right when Caedus was about to destroy the enemy fleet in a brilliant trap- the Jedi left the war, taking their StealthXs with them and turning the battle in the Confederation’s favor. A Jedi StealthX (by enderiac) It was here Caedus made a brilliant military decision. He withdrew the Fifth Fleet to Kashyyyk, a planet undecided in the war and hiding Jedi, who Caedus had now declared traitors. Caedus began to fire on Kashyyyk, burning the planet-wide and millennium-old Wroshyyyr forests to the ground. He hoped that he would force the Wookiees to surrender their sizable to the Alliance. He would then return to Kuat and turn the battle in the Alliance’s favor. He also knew, however, that this would not happen. The Confederation couldn’t allow him to get the Wookiee fleet, and allowing a potential Confederation member world to go up in flames would discourage other planets from joining their cause. He knew the Confederation would need to respond- and they did. Bothan and Corellian fleets left Kuat to engage the Fifth Fleet. Caedus fought back, and the fleets clashed above Kashyyyk. The Wookiee fleet arrived to help the Confederation, and to ake matters worse, the Hapans deserted Caedus, joining the large armada attacking the Fifth. Battle of Kashyyyk Now completely surrounded, the Fifth closed ranks on the Anakin Solo to protect it. Turbolaser strikes were blossoming against the Anakin Solo so frequently that those on the bridge couldn’t even see space, as so many turbolaser shots were blossoming against the shields that it looked like flashing lights. Gunners of the Fifth Fleet fired blind into the storm of bombardments, as sensors were overloaded by all the activity. Yet the Fifth, now on the verge of mutiny, made a bold move- they charged at the Bothan fleet, firing all their weapons at the Bothans. The Bothans, caught off guard, were convinced (with some help from Alema Rar and Caedus’ mind tricks) that Caedus wanted them to retreat, and so met Caedus’ charge with a counterattack of their own. This was a terrible mistake, as it opened a whole in the Confederation formation. The beleaguered Fifth Fleet, having taken enormous casualties, escaped the encirclement with only a third of their vessels operational. Yet despite their crushing defeat at Kashyyyk, Caedus was pleased. Though the Hapans and Wookiees had joined his uncle to form The Jedi Coalition, he had taken the battle away from the core and Coruscant. When Corellians and Bothans abandoned Kuat, forces under Cha Niathal were able to win the battle, securing the core and giving the Alliance some breathing room. When the Corellians did attack the core again, they found the Alliance ready and waiting. So, in conclusion, even though the Confederation and Jedi Coalition had one the battle, the fought the battle had been fought at all lost the war for them. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: Which was more powerful, Jacen Solo or Kylo Ren? Which got the better stories?

Question: What did the Second Galactic Civil War look like from a military perspective in Star Wars?
Answer: The Second Galactic Civil War is often thought about in flashpoints, such as the battle of Centerpoint or that of Shedu Maad. It’s also commonly viewed through the lens of the leaders who influenced the war, such as the joint leaders of the Galactic Alliance, Jacen Solo and Cha Nithal, or Gilead Paelleon of the Imperial Remnant. But the actual war- the campaigns and offensives- are often forgotten about or ignored. This is what I’ll be examining today. The Second Galactic Civil War began when the Galactic Alliance attempted to occupy a rebellious Corellia. Corellia repulsed the attack, and a GA blockade of the world was broken by Bothan and Commenonrian fleets coming to Corellia’s aide, creating the Confederation. The Skywalker-Solo family was initially split during the war- Han and Leia supported the Confederacy; Luke, Jacen, and Jaina supported the Alliance Now, more systems began joining Corellia’s rebellion. Alongside Corellia, Bothuwai, and Commenor stood the Hutts, Atzerri, Adumar, and Bespin. After halting a Confederation attempt to assassinate Tenel Ka at the Battle of Hapes, Galactic Alliance attempted to force a deceive battle against the Confederation before it got out of hand- but the Battle of Gilatter VII saw the Galactic Alliance fail to defeat a Confederation force. Luke, Lumiya, Leia, and Amela Rar duel The Confederation, smelling blood, launched an offensive into the core. Within weeks they neared the critical word of Kuat, who’s famed drive yards produced massive capital ships for the Alliance. Kuat Drive Yards The Kuat campaign was one of the bloodiest of the war. The Confederation set Hutt and Commenorian forces to harry the Republic’s flank at Balmorra while the better trained Bothan and Corellian forces attacked Kuat. Jacen Solo was able to defeat the Confederation forces at Balmorra, where he won a decisive victory- though at the cost of Balmorra itself. Yet Solo, who had turned to the Dark Side and became Darth Caedus, was unable to prevent the Bothan and Corellian forces from attacking Kuat. Outnumbered, Solo asked for allies- and the Hapans, fearful of their place in a Confederation-controlled galaxy- answered the call. The Hapes controlled a large fleet and massive amounts of credits Though the Hapans arrived to help the Galactic Alliance at Kuat, the battle was still mostly evenly matched. However, Caedus’s battle meditation allowed the GA to gain and edge- and by the end of the week he was on the edge of victory. Solo needed Jedi StealthXs to deal the finishing blow at Kuat However, at this point, the Jedi withdrew from the war, denying Caedus his victory at Kuat. With the battle rapidly turned against him, Caedus turned his gaze towards Kashyyyk. The Wookiees controlled an important hyperlane junction and a large fleet. If he attacked Kashyyyk, he would force the Confederation to draw off their attack at Kuat to go to Kashyyyk. The Battle of Kashyyyk rages Caedus arrived on Kashyyyk, and when the Wookiees refused to join him he began orbitally bombarding the planet, killing millions of wookiees. The Wookiees were on the verge of surrendering when Confederation forces arrived from Kuat to engage Caedus. The Wroshyyyr forests of Kashyyyk burn The Battle of Kashyyyk was a disaster for Caedus. The Hapan forces, shocked at what Caedus had done, arrived to support the Confederation fleet. Caedus’s forces were thoroughly thrashed, and the fifth fleet was only barely able to limp out of Kashyyyk in one piece. Meanwhile, the Jedi, Hapans, and Confederation signed a non aggression pact while they focused on their larger enemy- Caedus. Caedus’s actions at Kashyyyk set large swaths of the planet on fire. However, Caedus’ defeat at Kashyyyk wasn’t representative of the larger flow of the war. Caedus was eventually able to win at Kuat, and, spurred on by his legendary battle meditation- he launched into a devastating counterattack against the Confederation forces. He was able to force the Confederation out of the core and began attacks into their territory. Jacen Solo had also killed a defeated Mara Jade Becoming increasingly desperate, the Confederation asked for a truce. Caedus arrived to negotiate- but the Corellians used the lul in the fighting to activate Centerpoint Station, a superweapon based in the Corellian system. Centerpoint destroyed the Galactic Alliance Second Fleet- but more importantly, it destroyed any chance of a peaceful resolution to the war. Centerpoint Station Caedus attacked Centerpoint, hoping to capture it- and the Confederation responded, beginning a brutal battle in the space above Corellia. All while the Jedi Coalition- a new faction made up of the Jedi and Hapans, opposed to extremist elements on both sides, destroyed the station. The destruction of Centerpoint also unintentionally unleashed the ancient entity named Abeloth Countless ships from all sides were caught in the shockwave of Centerpoint’s destruction. Every side were injured, and needed allies. The Alliance found allies in the Imperial Remnant, the Confederation in the important world of Fondor, and the Jedi Coalition in Mandalorian Super Commandos lead by Boba Fett. The forces clashed at Fondor, where the GA split into two. Most forces backed Jacen Solo, with few joining Cha Nithal. Solo’s battle meditation was unparralled, allowing him to not just win individual battles, but to forsee entire galactic campaigns Following Fondor, Solo would begin a destructive campaign against his enemies. He defeated the Jedi at Roche, forcing them into hiding at Shedu Maad, contained Nithal’s forces around Fondor, and drove the Corellians into the brink of defeat. Cha Nithal But Luke Skywalker and Jaina Solo were able to lure Solo to Shedu Maad. Solo was killed by Jaina, and his fleet was torn to shreds by Hapan Battle Dragons and Mandalorian Commandos. The Confederation, Imperial Remnant, and Nithal’s forces surrendered unconditionally to the Jedi Coalition, ending the war. As Solo died, he opted not to kill his sister, instead deciding to warn his lover Tenel Ka about an impending nanovirus So, that is what happened during the Second Galactic Civil War. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: What is the most out of place piece of Star Wars content?
Answer: Star Wars: The Old Republic. For those of you who don’t know, 3600 years before the events of the original trilogy there was a massive series of wars between various factions, such as a resurgent Sith Empire, the Republic, and the forces of Zakuul. These forces were manipulated by Valkorion, the fourth most powerful mortal force user the galaxy would ever see. Firstly, the Great Galactic War, as it became known, is never mentioned in the lore. No one ever even talks about it. (Out of universe, this is because SWTOR was released after most of Legends.) The Great Galactic War was one of the largest conflicts in Star Wars- but is almost never mentioned in the lore. This wouldn't feel so out of place had similar events not been mentioned so often in Star Wars. Characters know and talk about the Great Hyperspace War, the Great Sith War, the Jedi Civil War, all less important events that happened prior to the Great Galactic War. But the Great Galactic War itself receives no mentions. This is true for Valkirion as well. Valkorion, only below Luke Skywalker, Darth Caedus, and Darth Sidious in power, is never mentioned in any holocron or by any Jedi. He never appears in any in universe history books, either. This same discrepancy plays out of universe as well. In sourcebooks and reference books, various events around that time period are fleshed out and detailed, but the Great Galactic War isn’t mentioned at all. I think the reason for this is because the writers of The Old Republic, known for a lack of originality, wanted to copy the Original Trilogy. So they made Valkorion as a ripoff Sidious, Malgus a ripoff Vader, and a massive war- while ignoring the plot holes that came with that. In conclusion, Star Wars: The Old Republic is very out of place within the Star Wars lore. Parts of it are awesome- had it been made a non canon game from the get-go perhaps it could have been alright. Sadly, it wasn’t. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: How did Ackbar turn the tide of the Yuuzhan Vong War?
Answer: Admiral Ackbar was able to turn the tide of the Yuuzhan Vong War. But firstly, we need to understand the New Republic’s situation in 28 ABY to understand how Ackbar was able to reverse it so dramatically. In 28 ABY the New Republic was on the brink of collapse. Within two years the extra-galactic invaders Yuuzhan Vong had smashed through the New Republic, taking Coruscant. In the next year, they smashed the New Republic defenses around the Southern Core and tightened their grip on the galaxy. In the Northern and Eastern quadrants, the Vong ruled. The New Republic, on the other hand, was a mess. Morale among fighting personal and civilians alike was at an all time low, the New Republic government has ceased to exist as a functioning entity. New Republic worlds seemed little more than hunting grounds for infidels to the Vong. Ackbar came out of retirement to lead the New Republic in this state. He immediately developed a plan, a series of minor strikes and engagements against the Vong. Ackbar would send fresh recruits on minor raids and missions to harry the Vong, and only when victory was certain. While these victories had little tactical value, they helped the New Republic in three important ways. Firstly, they kept the Vong occupied, preventing further incursions into New Republic space. Secondly, they tempered inexperienced New Republic troops for battle while suffering minimal casualties. Finally, they increased New Republic morale. For three years the galaxy’s newest apex predators had seemed unstoppable. Every New Republic victory against the Vong, no matter how minor, helped dispel that illusion. The New Republic launched raids at Gydine, Bimmisari, Wayland, Nal Hutta, Duro, and Ylesia. They were even able to win a major victory at Obroa-skai[1], destroying an important Yuuzhan Vong reserve fleet. Finally, when Ackbar was satisfied with his soldiers, he put the second part of his plan in motion. Ackbar leaked information to the Vong that the New Republic High Command were stationed at a space station on the planet Ebaq 9. Ackbar had a great understanding of Vong culture, knew that the Vong would take the bait and attack. When they did, he’d be waiting. The Vong attacked at Ebaq with their main war fleet, personally lead by their Warmaster Tsavong Lah, who’s tactical mind was as sharp as a lightsaber. Ackbar responded with his own fleet. He threw everything at the Vong- smugglers, Bothans, pirates, Jedi --- and won. The main Yuuzhan Vong War fleet was obliterated, trapped in low orbit above Ebaq under murderous fire. The few Vong ships that attempted to escape were destroyed by minefields. Tsavong Lah was defeated and killed in a deadly lightsaber duel with Jaina Solo. Though Ackbar would died after Ebaq, The battle turned the tide of the war. New Republic Chief of State Cal Omas, impressed by the victory, remade the New Republic into the Galactic Alliance. Omas wasn’t the only one impressed by the battle, either. In a series of diplomatic triumphs for the fledging alliance, the Hapans, Chiss, and Imperials joined the alliance. Within a year of Ebaq the war would be over. A Vong offensive against the Galactic Alliance was stalled at Dac, and the GA responded, thundering down the Perlimian Run. The Second Fleet crushed the Vong at Corulag, before most of the Galactic Alliance (including Hapan, Chiss, and Imperial elements) defeated the Vong over a captured Coruscant (renamed Yuuzhan’tar by the Vong), ending the war. GA forces establish air superiority over Galactic City during the Battle of Yuuzhan’Tar So, that is how Ackbar turned the tide of the war. Not only did he defeat the main Yuuzhan Vong War fleet, but his victory lead to the creation of the Galactic Alliance, the coalition that would win the war. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: What happened during the (SGCW) Battle of Fondor in Star Wars Legends?
Answer: The Battle of Fondor was one of the most important clashes of the Second Galactic Civil War, and it’s impacts were felt for decades to come. But in order to understand what happened and why it was so it important, we need to understand the battle’s backstory. Following the devestating Yuuzhan Vong War, the New Republic was reformed into the Galactic Alliance. However, tensions in the Alliance began to erupt over increased Corellian independance, and a war broke out between the Alliance and an increasing number of rebellious systems known as the Confederation, lead by Corellia. Han and Leia’s son, Jacen Solo, had fallen to the Dark Side and taken the moniker Darth Caedus, and the Mon Calamari Admiral Cha Nithal formed an alliance. They were able to launch a sucessful a coup to take over the Galctic Alliance. The two became Joint Chiefs of State, and lead the war effort against the Confederation. Cha Nithal Increasingly disgusted by the actions of the Galactic Alliance, which under the leadership of Jacen Solo had become increasingly totalitarian, the Jedi and Hapans withdrew from the war. This lead to a series of bloody clashes between the Galactic Alliance, Jedi and Hapan forces, and the Confederation at Kashyyyk, Balmorra, Kuat, and Centerpoint. The Anakin Solo fires on milenium old Wroshyyr forests during the Battle of Kashyyyk With both sides’ forces being worn down, the Confederation and Galactic Alliance were in search of new allies. Jacen Solo set his Sith apprentice, Tahiri Veila to Bastion, where he found an ally in Gilead Paelleon, the leader of the Imperial Remnant. They promised Paeelon the planets Bilbringi and Borelias in exchange for the Remnant’s support. Meanwhile, the Confederation found the support of the major shipbuilding world of Fondor. Realizing the importance of taking Fondor, Jacen Solo sent half of the Galactic Alliance fourth fleet to Fondor. Tahiri Veila also convinced Gilead Paelleon to send forces from the Imperial Remnant to help the Galactic Alliance. Gilead Paelleon Jacen Solo, Cha Nithal, and the Imperial Remnant arrived over Fondor, pushing throuigh the Confederation fleet before beginning to orbitally bombard the planet. Fondor surrendered, but Jacen Solo believed that Fondor hadn’t been punished enough. He refused to accept Fondor’s surrender, continuing to orbitally bombard Fondor’s cities, killing millions. Disgusted at Jacen’s actions, Cha Nihal attempted to relieve Solo of his command- but this backfired when two-thirds of the Alliance fleet joined Solo and began to engage Nithal’s forces. Gilead Paelleon, however, was equally disgusted with Jacen’s actions as Nithal, and so ordered his forces to join that of Nithal’s. This was in vain, however, as Paelleon was killed by Tahiri Veila, and the Imperial Remnant elected to join Solo. Tahiri Veila As Paelleon lay dying, the battle began heavily turning against Nithal, as she was badly outnumbered. However, Paelleon commed his old friend Natasi Daala, who had been building up her forces in the Maw Installation for decades. Daala, who’s forces were equipped with Metal-Crystal Phase Shifters, joined the battle on Nithal’s side. Natasi Daala The suprise of Daala’s entry into the battle (Daala was thought dead at the Battle of Columus over 20 years ago) and her Metal-Crystal Phase Shifters (which could pentrate shields) were able to turn the battle against Caedus. He was forced to retreat, though Nithal’s forces had taken heavy casualties. Jacen Solo during the battle Ultimately, however, the battle furthered Caedus’ plans. Though Caedus had been forced to retreat from the battlefield, he was now in complete control of the Galactic Alliance, and had the loyalty of the Imperial Remnant. This would lead to Caedus’ push against the Jedi and Hapan coalition, and lead to the fateful Battle of Shedu Maad, where the fate of the war would be decided. So, that is what happened at the Battle of Fondor, and why it was so important. Stay safe, -Ben

More importantly, however, they had stood their ground and won in a capital ship engagement for the first time. So, in conclusion, the Rebel Alliance’s biggest victory before Yavin was the Battle of Turkana in Legends. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: What Star Wars villain wasn't actually evil?
Answer: Darth Caedus. Darth Caedus, born Jacen Solo, the son of Han and Leia, became a Sith Lord in 40 ABY during the opening stages of the Second Galactic Civil War. Though Caedus committed many evil actions during the war, such as murdering Prince Isolder and burning the forests of Kashyyyk to the ground, his actions had good intentions and actually made the galaxy a better place. In order to demonstrate this, it’s important to explain why Caedus joined the Sith. See, Jacen Solo had multiple visions. The first was off the galaxy erupting into the flames of eternal war, and his uncle, Luke Skywalker, lying dead. The second saw the evil Darth Krayt sitting on the Throne of Balance, with Solo’s daughter, Allana Solo, at Krayt’s side. Darth Krayt Solo sought to stop these visions from becoming a reality. He launched a campaign against the Corellian rebels, winning numerous battles in the Second Galactic Civil War. These actions were effective in preventing his vision from becoming a reality. His daughter never fell to the dark side, eternal war was prevented, and Darth Krayt noted his plans for galactic domination were delayed 80 years by Caedus’ actions. I’d also like to quote Legacy of the Force: Tempest, which explain’s Caedus’ POV pretty well. He could never stop trying to bring peace and order to the galaxy… that Allana and all the children like her deserved to grow up on worlds untroubled by war and injustice. (pg. 153–154) In conclusion, Darth Caedus wasn’t actually evil- in fact, his actions delayed the Darth Krayt’s galactic takeover for 80 years. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: Did George Lucas hate Star Wars Legends?
Answer: No. A lot of people will claim that Lucas hated Star Wars Legends. This could not be further from the truth. George Lucas actually greatly enjoyed Star Wars Legends- according to Dave Filoni, he called it “fun and exciting.[1]” And what’s more, Lucas supported Star Wars Legends several times. He worked closely in the development of the New Jedi Order series, he put Aayla Secura (who was previously introduced in a comic) into Attack of the Clones, and he apparently even gave copies of Dark Empire out as Christmas gifts to his employees. We also get this quote from an interview with Minixmojo Mixnmojo: "How much of a role does George Lucas have in the day-to-day activities of LucasArts? Tim Schafer once described him 'coming to visit' the team during the making of The Secret of Monkey Island in 1990, and offering his advice on the title. Was he involved in the decision to revisit it?" Mary Bihr: "Definitely. George is involved at a high level with everything we do. He approves and gives feedback on all projects, concepts and stories." In conclusion, it’s pretty clear that George Lucas did approve of and enjoy Star Wars Legends. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: Is Admiral Ackbar really better than Thrawn? What are each one's strengths and weaknesses?
Answer: Yes, in Legends Ackbar is the superior admiral. This is demonstrated by each admiral’s strengths and weaknesses. Thrawn’s greatest weakness was when third-party or irregular forces would disrput his carefully laid plans. During the battle of Sluis Van, Lando Calrissian’s mole miners delivered one of Thrawn’s first defeats. At Bilbringi, he was assassinated by his bodyguard Rukh. Ackbar’s only weakness, however, was how good he was. The Essential Guide to Warfare notes “If Ackbar had a weakness, it was that he was irreplaceable.” (pg. 182) Now, Ackbar’s greatest strength was his ability to work with others. Ackbar was the father of the Alliance fleet, and he wielded it as if it was an extension of his own body. Ackbar united the various rebel leaders in 1 BBY and would combine small rebel cells into the Alliance fleet. In addition, Ackbar commanded great respect among his soldiers, and his return to the New Republic in 27 ABY during the Yuuzhan Vong War sparked widespread celebration on New Republic vessels. A large part of this was due to Ackbar’s willingness to work and understand his subordinates at a level that truly mattered. In the Young Jedi Knights: The Lost Ones, we see Ackbar piloting a transport to get a better understanding of how the New Republic navy functioned at its most basic level. This also helped command respect among his subordinates. Thrawn’s greatest strength was his ability to exploit the weaknesses of others. At the Battle of Obroa-Skai, Thrawn was able to exploit the fact that his opponent was an Elom to win the battle. This ability is certainly quite powerful and effective. However, it’s also something Ackbar does much better. In Legacy of the Force: Tempest, Admiral Nek Bwua’tu states that only Ackbar could exploit his enemy’s weakness so masterfully- putting Ackbar directly above Thrawn in that category. In conclusion, yes, Ackbar is clearly much better than Thrawn. I’ll also link a doc fulling breaking down each of the admiral’s feats and quotes if you want a more expansive answer. Stay safe, -Ben

A powerful warship created during the New-class Modernization Program, the Majestic was heavily armed and shielded against capital ships and starfighters- and even had room for five snubfighter squadrons. Question: What was the most unique way of capturing a planet in Star Wars?
Answer: Convincing some shareholders to give it to you willingly has to be up there. This tactic was used during the taking of Kuat in 8 ABY. Kuat was one of the most important planets in galaxy. It’s planet-spanning dockyards pumped out many Star Destroyers for the Empire, and the other factions that controlled it. As a result, it was an important target for the New Republic. However, previous assaults had been foiled by adversaries such as Boba Fett and Zsinj. However, after Zsinj’s defeat in 8 ABY, and the weakening of the Empire that followed it, the New Republic sought to take advantage of the Empire’s state and take Kuat. However, Kuat’s defenses were formidable. It was guarded by more than a dozen Star Destroyers, 3 battlecruisers, and even the half-complete Eclispe Super Star Destroyer, not to mention powerful orbital defenses. Knowing that an assault on Kuat would be very costly, the New Republic devised a different plan. For months, they painstakingly added astromechs to KDY’s droid pool. When all droids were in, the astromechs gave five Star Destroyers a virus, including the battlecruiser Event Horizon then erased all evidence of the virus’ existence. Then, a squadron of A-Wings lead by Tycho Celchu- nicknamed Surprise Squadron and outfitted with experimental ion bombs- jumped into the system and hit several Star Destroyers with ion bombs. While the damaged Star Destroyers tried to get their systems back on line, the infected Star Destroyers turned their turbolasers on some of the other Star Destroyers in the system. At this point, the New Republic hailed KDY (the company that controlled Kuat) with a curious demand- a sharehold meeting. Since the fall of the Empire, KDY’s stock had been essentially valueless for years- and several companies secretly under New Republic control had bought up 34% of the shares in KDY. The New Republic pointed out that within minutes, 9 Star Destroyers had been knocked out of action. Besides they had several task forces just outside of Kuat, while the nearest Imperial task force was days away. Although Kateel of Kuhlvult, the CEO of KDY, said that Kuat would not surrender, 3 shareholders controlling a combined 18% of the shares voted to surrender. Kateel of Kuhlvult was forced to oblidge, and the Imperial forces at Kuat were allowed to retreat to Orinda. But there were other forces at work too, and the New Republic’s victory was not complete. Within hours of Kuat’s surrender, Imperial agents rammed two battlecruisers, the Aurora and Stellar Halo, into Kuat’s sun. They then abducted several important KDY designers, before fleeing to the Deep Core on the half complete Eclipse. The Eclispe So, in conclusion, the taking of Kuat was a unique way to take a planet. Stay safe, -Ben

Space Marines, Void Jumpers, and Jedi launched an effort to retake the Jedi Temple. This battle was as devastating as it was important. A Jedi infiltration team planned to destroy the Temple’s shields while Space Marines attacked the outside. The plan worked, and that allowed Void Jumpers to enter the Temple via paradrop. The Void Jumpers forced the Sith out of the Temple from the inside, making the fight spill into Fellowship Plaza. Sith saboteurs, fleeing the temple, began to destroy skyscrapers across the planet. Meanwhile, Abeloth destroyed the Galactic Justice Center, which was being used by the Space Marines as a field hospital, before causing massive volcanic eruptions across Coruscant. These eruptions caused lava flows that collapsed thousands of skyscrapers, killing billions. Picture this plus Mustafar In conclusion, during the post Endor era Coruscant was a pretty terrible place to live in. Stay safe, -Ben

Name: Ben Choucroun
Question: What's one thing canon gets wrong in Star Wars?
Answer: Ship prices. Now, this might seem strange, but ship prices in canon are very inconsistent. When it comes to the cost of Star Wars ships, it seems like the canon writers just spin a wheel and get their answer. Let’s look at some of the most egregious examples. Imperial Star Destroyers cost 150 million credits. We’ll use this as our baseline, as it is a reasonable price taken from Legends. We’ll see how similar ships compare to this. The Interdictor Star Destroyer is a ship slightly shorter than an ISD. However, it comes equipped with expensive gravity well generators. It costs 15 million credits. Let that sink in. A Interdictor Star Destroyer costs 1/10th as much as a regular Star Destroyer. An even worse example is the Starhawk. The Starhawk is much larger and more powerful than an ISD- however, it only costs 60 million credits. Now, the Starhawk does use parts from an ISD- but remember, it needs two Imperial Star Destroyers in order for it to be built, making its price non-sensical. Not to mention the fact that disassembling 2 entire Star Destroyers is certain to cost more than 60 million credits. Another example would be the U-Wing. Normally, an average fighter with shields and life support costs around 150,000. However, the U-Wing only costs 65,000 credits, the price of a TIE Fighter, despite having shields, life support, and heavier weapons. I’d lastly like to note the Providence-class Destroyer. Despite being over 600 meters shorter than an Imperial Star Destroyer, and having significantly less weaponry, it costs almost three times as much as an ISD. In conclusion, it seems that in canon, authors just kind of make stuff up with no sort of logical consistency. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: How does the First Order in the sequel trilogy compare to the Imperial Remnant from Star Wars Legends?
Answer: Like usual, Legends is vastly superior to canon in this aspect. In canon, the First Order makes no real sense. Apparently they were created by Imperials who fled the Empire after their defeat, which is fine and all except that Palpatine orchestrated the Empire’s defeat for no discernable reason[1]. We also know that somehow the First Oder attacked the galaxy and took it over within literally a day. They somehow defeated the entire New Republic military and reigned over the galaxy within 24 hours of their assault on Hosnian Prime, which is implausible at best. Yet while the First Order’s plotholes are certainly numerous, their worst fault in my opinion lies with their lack of depth. The First Order is pretty much the same as the Empire. There isn’t really a change in doctrine. Like many things in the sequels, or Season 4 of Arrested Development, it’s a copy of what came before it, but without the magic that made the original series stand out. Compare this to the Imperial Remnant, however. The Remnant isn’t just generic space Nazis. The Imperial Remnant after Endor dissolves into dozens of squabbling warlords and various factions vying for control- which makes much more sense than almost all the Empire immediately rallying around one leader like in canon. Back to Legends. The Imperial Remnant’s story is featured in inconic stories like the Thrawn Trilogy, the New Jedi Order, and Fate of the Jedi. These are all amazing stories that are well told. However, the First Order’s story in canon is told by… Aftermath and the Sequel Trilogy. One part I like about the Imperial Remnant in Legends is what they do after they make peace with the New Republic. The Imperial Remnant, after the Paelleon-Gavrisom treaty that ended the Galactic Civil War, becomes a functioning state ruled by sympathetic leaders. And this, in my opinion, is why the Imperial Remnant in Legends is much better than the First Order in canon. The Imperial Remnant, while it does have growing pains while trying to become a democratic state, legitimately does what they believe is best for the galaxy. They have responsible leaders like Gilead Paelleon, Jagged Fel, and Vitor Riege. Meanwhile, the First Order is ruled by a resurrected Palpatine strandcast or something. It has no serious ideological difference from the Empire and is basically space Nazis 2.0. In conclusion, the First Order is a pale imitation of the Imperial Remnant from Legends. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: If you have a billion credits to construct a fleet in Star Wars, what ships would you buy?
Answer: First off, some ground rules. I won’t be including pay for the crew or consumables like ammunition and food in this count. I’ll also be using on pre-NJO ships- so no StealthXs, for example, as well as Legends only. Finally, I’ll only use ships we have a definitive price for. I’ll start by buying one Nebula-class Star Destroyer. These ships are absolute beasts, and it would be my flagship. These ships, while only a kilometer long, can easily take on and defeat a Star Destroyer. My main Star Destroyer would be the Republic-class Star Destroyer. While slightly weaker than an Imperial II Star Destroyer, its only half the cost. I’ll purchase five of these for a combined cost of 375 million credits, with 625 million left to spend. I would also include a couple heavy cruisers. I’ll pick two Bothan Assault Cruisers. These ships can add a fair bit of extra firepower to our arsenal, however, their primary role is to plug up any gaps in our formation if they occur, and to hold our flanks. For my frigate, I’ll take 10 MC-30 frigates. These ships are better armed than the Nebulon B, and have great shields. These ships are great multi-purpose ships, being able to ward off capital ships and defend against starfighters. They also come equipped with cluster bombs. I’ll take ten of these at 9,500,000 each. For my corvette I’ll pick the CR-92 Corvette. These ships are cheaper and better armed than CR-90s, and will be used to ward off starfighetrs and tangle with larger capital ships. I’ll take fourteen of these for 2,500,000 apiece. I’ll then buy a quartet of DP-20 frigates for 4,800,000 each. These ships will be used to finish off damaged enemy vessels. Their high speed and reasonable shields allow them to launch hit and run attacks on enemy vessels as well. I’ll also buy 12 Skipray Blastboats for 285,000 each. These ships will be used to ward off enemy fighters. Sadly, wanted to buy some Warrior-class Gunboats instead of these- but lacking a definitive price for the Warrior, I sacrificed the firepower of the Warrior for the anti-starfighter capabilities of the Skipray. For starfighters, I’ll purchase the E-Wing as my fighter (160,000 per fighter), K-Wing as my bomber (250,000), and A-Wings as my interceptors (175,000). All are excellent craft, with the K-Wing in particular standing out among them. I’ll buy 4 wings of E-Wings, as well as 2 wings of K-Wings and 2 wings of E-Wings. After that, we have 53 million credits remaining. I’ll spend 900,000 to get 4 YM-2800 Limpet Ships. These ships can latch on to enemy ships, send in borders to take the bridge, vent the oxygen to the rest of the ship, and use the now captured enemy vessel against its former owners. Finally, I’ll purchase a black market Immobilizer 418 cruiser for just over 52 million credits. This will prevent our enemy from escaping. I’ll also purchase a Punworcca 116-class interstellar sloop as my personal starship just for the memes. This will leave me with just over 3,000 credits to spend on whatever. Perhaps I’ll purchase a datapad and a news subscription to stay up to current evens in the galaxy, or spend my money on deathsticks in a shady Nar Shadda Bar. So, in conclusion, if I had a billion credits I’d buy 1 Nebula-class Star Defender, 5 Republic-class Star Destroyers, 2 Bothan Assualt Cruisers, 10 MC-30 cruisers, 14 CR-90 corvettes, 4 DP-20 frigates, 12 Skipray Blastboats, 144 E-Wings, 72 K-Wings, 72 A-Wings, an Immobilizer 418 cruiser, 4 YM-2800 Limpet Ships, and a Punworcca 116-class interstellar sloop. I’m fairly confident that this fleet could defeat the other ships in this answer in battle. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: What do you think of the Galaxy Fleet in the Rise of Skywalker?

The time between the Falcon left for Pasanna and the time the Galaxy Fleet arrived at Exegol is 16 hours. I think a safe estimate for the trips to Pasana and Kijimis is about 8 hours. That means that in 8 hours minimum (keep in mind travelling through hyperspace takes up time as well) Lando was able to create a fleet with 14,000 battle ready capital ships. The fact that there are so many capital ships available doesn’t make sense. We learn in the Aftermath Trilogy that keeping a Star Destroyer even semi-operational is incredibly expensive, even for a crime lord. So the idea that thousands of private citizens owned capital ships is pretty implausible. Finally, the fleet composition doesn’t make sense. Among others, we see an absolute ton of Virgillian Bunker Busters, Sullustan Freighters, Lothalian Corvettes, and Mon Calamari star cruisers. However, these ships are all from planets in the Outer Rim, while Lando went to the core. And the First Order doesn’t allow cross-galactic travel. So how did these ships come to Lando’s call. The Mon Calamari cruiser at the bottom looks like the dreaded lovechild of an MC-90 cruiser and Crossfire fighter. Also, a Pelta. While this isn’t an inconsistency or anything, I do wish the movie had been more specific about what part of the Core Lando went to. The Core is a big place. Did Lando go to the Northern Core, where Coruscant, Metellos, and Anaxes are? Did he go to the Arrowhead, where planets like Ruan, Kuat, and Balmorra lay. Or perhaps the Southern Core, where you can find Fondor, Corellia, Duro, and Nubia. Art by Stephen Zavala In conclusion, the Galaxy Fleet in the Rise of Skywalker doesn’t make sense. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: What is the most underrated Star Wars book series?

Name: Ben Choucroun
Question: How did the New Republic lose the Battle of Fondor during the Yuuzhan Vong War?
Answer: In order to understand the Battle of Fondor, we must first understand the factions involved. There are four major players: The New Republic and the Yuuzhan Vong are well known, the New Republic being the major galactic government and the Vong being the nihilistic invading enemy force. The Hutts are the Hutts, a massive criminal empire that controls a region of space in the Outer Rim. And the Hapes Consortium is a small but very powerful monarchy located in the Inner Rim. The leadup to Fondor begins after the Yuuzhan Vong take Gyndine. There, they make an alliance with the Hutts. The Vong will spare Hutt worlds if the Hutts allow the Vong to operate in Hutt Space. The Hutts agree, with the sole condition that the Vong tell the Hutts what planets they will attack so the Hutts can stop shipping spice to those planets, so the Hutts don’t lose any planets. The Vong tell the Hutts that they will attack Tynna, Corellia, and Bothuwai. The Hutts immediately tell the New Republic. Meanwhile, the New Republic allies itself with the Hapes Consortium. The Hapes pledge their considerable wealth and fleet to the New Republic, and leave for Commenor. The Vong take Tynna, meeting little resistance. The New Republic now believes the Hutts and think that the Vong will attack Bothuwai or Corellia. What’s more, the New Republic has an ace up its sleeve. Anakin Solo helps reactivate Centerpoint Station, an ancient superweapon based in Corellia that can fire hyperspace beams across the galaxy. The New Republic plans to use it against the Vong. They move their Corellian forces to Bothawui, hoping that an unguarded Corellia will present a tempting offer to the Vong. The New Republic hopes that the Vong will attack Corellia, where they will be destroyed by Centerpoint Station. However, Senator Viqi Shesh of Kuat is actually a Yuuzhan Vong spy. She tells the Vong of both the Hutt’s treachery and to not attack Corellia. The Vong then tell the Hutts to resume their spice shipments to Bothuwai, which the Hutts immediately tell to the New Republic. This makes the New Republic even more confident that the Vong will attack Corellia. Question: What Star Wars battle was really important but is almost never talked about?
Answer: In Legends, the Second Battle of Obroa-Skai. Unless you’re a really big Star Wars EU fan, you’ve probably never heard of the Second Battle of Obroa-Skai. Essentially, it took place during the Yuuzhan Vong War shortly after Operation Emperor’s Spear and the Fall of Coruscant. The Second Battle of Obroa-Skai was a really important battle, however, it only gets a footnote in Galactic History. This battle saw X-Wings under Rogue Squadron and Kyp’s Dozen, along with capital ships under Keyan Farlander, as well as Hapan forces under Tenel Ka, destroy a large Vong fleet under commander Komm Krash. This battle was important for four reasons. First off, it saw the first use of Yammosk Jammers. The extra-galactic invaders the Yuuzhan Vong employed war coordinators, called jammers. The New Republic had created a Yammosk Jammer to stop the Yammosk’s ability to coordinate Yuuzhan Vong fleets, however, it had become ineffective. The New Republic realized they were using a second Yammosk and so employed a second Yammosk Jammer for the first time, which was crucial in their victory. Yammosks like the one above coordinated the Vong effort, and allowed Vong ships to have a level of coordination similar to that granted by battle melds. Second off, the fleet under Komm Krash was the last Yuuzhan Vong extra-galactic reserve fleet. By destroying it, the Vong could expect no further reinforcements- which seriously hurt Yuuzhan Vong morale. Thirdly, it helped New Republic morale immensely. Obroa-Skai was a world of cultural significance to the New Republic, as it held the largest libraries in the galaxy. By retaking it, the New Republic not only showed that the Vong weren’t unbeatable but they also reclaimed an important planet. Finally, this was the first time Hapans and the New Republic had worked together since the disastrous Battle of Fondor. This combined victory helped build respect and trust between the two allies- something that would be needed for the upcoming Battle of Coruscant. Above: The Hapan Navy In conclusion, the Second Battle of Obroa-Skai was one of the most important battles of the Yuuzhan Vong War- but it is rarely mentioned. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: What are some of the best examples of foreshadowing in the Star Wars prequels?
Answer: There are a bunch of great examples of foreshadowing in the prequels. In this answer, I’ll try to cover my favorite examples without touching on examples that are either really obvious (Why do I feel you’re gonna be the death of me) or ones I covered before (links to those answers below). One great example is when Jango Fett says “They do their job well, I guarantee that.” This, of course, foreshadows Order 66, in which the clone troopers do a great job of wiping out the Jedi. It’s a simple line, and one often overlooked- but it foreshadows the destruction of the Jedi Order. Another example is when Anakin says “I can’t breathe” to Padmé. While this line is often made fun of, it foreshadows Return of the Jedi when Luke removes Anakin’s mask and Anakin can’t breathe. Palpatine’s servants also represent what Anakin will become. Maul represents anger and hatred, Dooku represents leaving the Jedi Order, and Grievous represents the cyborg Anakin will become. The way the Jedi are chained up on Geonosis represents Anakin’s conflicting loyalties in Revenge of the Sith- he’s being torn between his wife and the Jedi Order. Next up, we have Padmé’s outfit in Attack of the Clones. George Lucas wanted this outfit to symbolize how she was being metaphorically choked- and she would be physically choked three years later by Anakin. Finally, we have Qui-Gon’s line in The Phantom Menace “There’s always a bigger fish.” While this may seem innocuous at first, it is actually foreshadowing how there’s always a bigger and badder Sith: Maul, Dooku, and then Palpatine. So, those are some of the best examples of foreshadowing in the prequels. Stay safe, -Ben

The droids are fairly stupid and aren’t very smart- we see their incompetence displayed multiple times in the trilogy. Their opponents, clones, however, are living, human beings, who can think. So what Obi-Wan is really saying is that if they fight a living opponent that could think independently and could be deployed in large numbers, they would wipe out the Jedi. And, one movie later, that is exactly what happens. So, in conclusion, when Obi-Wan said "If droids could think, there'd be none of us here,” he was foreshadowing Vader, Grievous, and Order 66. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: If the Yuuzhan Vong had become active thirty years earlier, how would they have fared against the Galactic Empire?
Answer: They would have been defeated fairly quickly. See, there are multiple advantages that the Empire has when dealing with the Vong. The first is that the Empire doesn’t care about casualties or destroying the environment. Why is this important? Well, the Empire could carry out a scorched earth tactic. See, the Yuuzhan Vong use organic technology. This technology has to be grown on a planet. If the Galactic Empire renders every planet they retreat from uninhabitable with radiation, the Vong are screwed as they can’t make any new ships. Second off, the New Republic Advisory Council was a mess of various influences- from the Jedi hating Fyor Rodan of Commenor to the treasonous Pwoe from Dac to the infamous Borsk Fey’la. This slowed down the war effort and hindered the ability of the Jedi Knights. For example, the New Republic senate didn’t acknowledge the threat until months after the Praetorite Vong had invaded. The Empire had no such bureaucracy. They had one authoritarian leader who would use any and all means at his disposal to defeat the Vong, whether it be through overwhelming force or the scorched earth tactics mentioned above. Finally, the Empire had better starfighters for the job. The Empire used TIEs, which on paper are worse than X and E-Wings. However, Coralskippers used miniature black holes to absorb laser shots, meaning that it was a good idea to overwhelm them with shots coming from different directions. TEI Fighters are ideal for this. And this shows, too. During the early stages of the war the New Republic attempted to lure the Vong into a decisive fleet battle, which turned into defeat after defeat. But at Ithor the Imperial Remnant stood and fought-and won, too. But Deign Lian unleashed a bio-weapon on Ithor, and Corran Horn, the Jedi, and the Remnant took the blame. Lastly, I’m not defending the Empire. They’re evil, obviously, and just particularly well equipped to fight the Vong. And no, Palpatine did not build the Empire/anything in it to fight the Vong Stay safe, -Ben

Name: Ben Choucroun
Question: How come in the Star Wars universe, the technology is more advanced in prequels than originals?
Answer: That isn’t the case. In the Original Trilogy we see 6 main planets- Tatooine, Yavin, Hoth, Dagobah, Bespin, and Endor. While most of these are not technologically advanced, this makes perfect sense. See, the Original Trilogy takes place in the Outer Rim. This part of the galaxy was technologically behind the core worlds, and as a result is less technologically developed. This is alluded to when Luke says “If there's a bright center to the universe, you're on the planet that it's farthest from.” Plus, over half of the locations we see in the Original Trilogy are mostly uninhabited. Yavin is hidden, secret base, as is Hoth. Endor is inhabited by teddy bears, and Dagobah has a ketamine-fueled frog with terrible grammar. Do you expect these places to have skyscrapers like Coruscant? Finally on our planets list, we have Bespin. Bespin is very technologically advanced. It's literally a massive city hanging in the clouds that’s 400 stories high. Making that is pretty impressive, and is arguably more impressive than anything in the prequels. When it comes to ships, remember that the Rebel Alliance used anything they could find. They stole their Y-Wings bombers and made their X-Wings in suboptimal conditions. The Empire, on the other hand, emphasized fear. Their ships emulated this, by using strong shapes and dark designs instead of sleek edges like on the Naboo fighter. It's also important to remember, when discussing the droid army, that in the Original Trilogy, that it wouldn’t make sense for either faction to use droids. The droid army terrorized the galaxy, and so whoever used them would be villainized in the public eye. The prequels, on the other hand, spend much of their time in the Galactic Core. Here is where most of the credits in the galaxy wind up, and so it is more technologically advanced. The times we do leave we often go to wealthy planets, such as Naboo (whose plasma deposits made them rich) or planets with massive populations (like Geonosis) whose population has the ability to make massive catacombs. Furthermore. The ships we see in the prequels are often direct predecessors of ships in the Original Trilogy. The ARC-170 evolves into the X-Wing, the Venator-class Star Destroyer evolves into the Imperial-class Star Destroyer, and the AT-RT evolves into the AT-ST. In conclusion, the technology of the Prequels often is behind that shown in the Original Trilogy- and when it's not, it makes sense. Stay safe, -Ben *Another answer also noted that Luke’s Prosthetic hand is much advanced than Anakin’s

Name: Ben Choucroun
Question: Why are space battles so common and ground battles so rare in Star Wars?
Answer: Because space is the ultimate high ground. In Star Wars, having space basically gives you control over the planet. The first reason for this is that by controlling space, you can orbitally bombard areas of land. An army passing through an unpopulated region without control of the space above it is basically dead, as enemy ships can just launch turbolasers. The Assertor-class Star Dreadnought Wrath commences a Base Delta Zero (orbital bombardment) strike This means, with the exception of unique planets like Mon Calamari or Coruscant, (where orbital bombardment is ineffective) you can’t really have non-guerrilla/insurgent force, as it will get wiped out immediately. Next up, having control of space also means that you have fighter superiority. This means you can send in ships to take down enemy targets from the air. X-Wings, for example, can take out AT-ATs. Finally, controlling space means you control trade coming in and out. On planets like Brentaal or Coruscant, which are heavily reliant on trade, losing control of space means you lose any food imports. So, that is why controlling space in Star Wars is so important, and why there aren’t often large ground battles. This also brings up probably one of my biggest problems with the prequels- why not use air support/orbital bombardment? Stay safe, -Ben

Question: What did the Imperials do with captured Rebel prisoners?
Answer: The Imperials didn’t torture or execute Rebel prisoners. In fact, what they did in Legends was genius. What the Empire did was turn Rebel prisoners into Imperial sleeper agents and then release them to rejoin the Alliance, saying they escaped. For example, the Mon Calamari Terpfen was captured, reprogrammed, and made into an Imperial Sleeper Agent who tried to assassinate Admiral Ackbar. However, the Alliance slowly began to catch on to this. So what the Imperials would do is reprogram only a few Alliance agents, while allowing many other soldiers that they did not reprogram to escape. This caused Alliance bases to have to either reject all escaped prisoners (some of whom were friends of people working at the base) or risk taking in sleeper agents. This dramatically lowered overall Alliance morale. In canon, the Empire did a similar thing. They reprogrammed captured prisoners on Ashmead's Lock, then released them to the New Republic. Question: Could the CIS have won the Clone Wars without Sidious's machinations?
Answer: Almost certainly. See, the CIS had several massive advantages in the Clone Wars that they could have used to win the war had Darth Sidious not stopped them. The first comes to infantry soldiers. A B1 battle droid can be produced in 10 minutes using minimal amounts of material. A clone takes 10 years to grow and requires food, water, clothing, and shelter during that time. Although a clone is much more effective than a droid, CIS droid armies could simply overwhelm clones- and the CIS had quadrillions of droids. Next up, the CIS had an economic advantage. Most factory worlds and worlds that produced raw material joined the CIS- and this really hurt the economy of the Republic. This, coupled with how expensive it was to make clones, gave the CIS a massive fiscal advantage. Finally, the Republic, at least in the early days of the war, had only one place where they could make clones- Kamino. If the Separatists destroyed Kamino, the war would be over. In fact, a CIS strike at Kamino was foiled by Darth Sidious as he didn’t want one side to win easily. So, in conclusion, the CIS could easily win the Clone Wars if they weren’t hindered by Darth Sidious. In fact, Hirib Bassot* (a pundit and podcaster) noticed this in the waning days of the Clone Wars. He pointed out Any coalition capable of producing even quadrillions of any machine could roll over the Republic in a few days. Stay safe, -Ben *Bassot was found dead in his home just days after pointing this out

Another book I love is Rebel Dream, the first book in the Enemy Lines Duology. (The second book, Rebel Stand, is great as well, but it is less of a war novel). Anyway, this book covers the Battle of Borelias and the fallout from the f all of Coruscant. Not only is it well written, but the way they cover the dynamic in the New Republic after the fall of Coruscant is handled quite well. There are other such books that would fall into this category as well that I have varying degrees of fondness for. I do enjoy Darksaber, Shadows of Mindor is fine, and I dislike Republic Commadno. However, the ultimate “military book” is the Essential Guide to Warfare. This is one of my favorite Star Wars books, and I have read it at least a dozen times. I would highly recommend it. In canon, the only one that comes to mind is the Battlefront (2015) book. I really enjoyed it actually, being one of the few good (or even passable) canon books out there. It covers the 61st Mobile Infantry company and is a pretty harsh, yet enthralling, read. It really made me nostalgic for the Rebel Alliance Sourcebook while reading it. So, those are the most military like books in Star Wars. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: In Star Wars, what made Ackbar an effective commander?
Answer: His ability to work with his subordinates. Much has been said about Ackbar’s tactical brilliance. From a sheer strategic level, he was probably a better tactician than Thrawn himself[1]. Futhermore, he had a great command of administrative and technical details, serving as project lead of the MC-90 Battlecruiser, the Viscount Star Defender, and the B-Wing starfighter. But what made Ackbar truly great was how he worked with his subordinates, and how that allowed him to have an excellent grasp of how the New Republic navy worked. For example, in the Legends book Young Jedi Knights: The Lost Ones, we see Ackbar piloting the bulk cruiser Adamant to a get a better understanding of how the navy functions on a basic level- something other admirals would likely never do. And this pays off as well. In addition to making Ackbar a better admiral, it also drastically increased morale in his soldiers, too. To quote Destiny’s Way, Three hours after the end of the meeting, the message ACKBAR IS BACK was broadcast to all New Republic military units. On some of the larger ships, the cheering lasted for an hour. So, in conclusion, Ackbar’s ability to work with his subordinates truly made him the best admiral in Galactic History. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: Are there any ways to tell whether someone is force sensitive?
Answer: There are four methods which can be used to tell whether someone is force sensitive. The first is the most obvious- midichlorian tests. These calculate the amount of midichlorians per cell in someone’s body. Normal people will have around 2,500 midichlorians per cell, however, Anakin Skywalker had excess of over 20,000. The next is via a force scanning device belonging to Emperor Palpatine, and more broadly, Thaissen crystals. See, these crystals glowed blue around a light side user and red around a dark side user. These were put in a device and Palpatine, Luke and Brakiss, used this device to find force-sensitives. The next is a slightly unethical practice developed by Luke Skywalker. He would reach into people’s minds and try to feel their memories of something. If that person fought them off, such as Leia and Kyp Durron did, they were force sensitive. Finally, you could watch them and see if they use the force subconsciously. Anakin’s superior reflexes granted to him by the force allowed him to be the only human podracer. Or perhaps they get a bit too lucky in the casino. So, that is how you can determine whether someone is force-sensitive. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: In Legends, the New Republic captured two SSDs. Did the New Republic capture any in Star Wars canon?

Question: Is being force-sensitive actually a curse in the Star Wars universe?
Answer: It can be. See, during the Age of the Empire, being force-sensitive was kind of a curse. This was because, if you were found, you would face one of several unpleasant possibilities. And being found was likely, as the Empire had scanners to detect force sensitives[1]. The first possibility you might face was being killed outright. If you were strong in the force, Palpatine would want you killed so you wouldn’t pose a threat to his regime. This was especially likely if you were a non-human, due to the Human High Culture in the Empire. The second possibility was that you would be invited to become an Inquisitor/Dark Side Adept. This was generally not fun for a number of reasons. For one, they are generally fodder for main characters. For another, you had to use the dark side and were often subjected to brutal training. And finally, if you didn’t join them you would be killed. In Legends, Kam Solusar was captured and brutally tortured by the Inquistorius, eventually becoming a Dark Side agent before turning back to the light Finally, you might be subjected to various tests and tortures. Palpatine conducted many hideous experiments on many force sensitives. One such victim of these experiments was Tricolus, who became a three eyed mutant[2]. So, in conclusion, being force-sensitive was a bit of curse during the Rise of the Empire. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: What is the difference between the Galactic Republic and the Old Republic?
Answer: Galactic Republic and Old Republic are used a lot, and it can be confusing to tell which time period is being talked about when these terms are used. Galactic Republic was generally used to discuss the Republic during the prequel area from 1,000 BBY to 19 BBY. It was also used during the New Republic era to talk about the New Republic. People in the prequel era referred to the time before 1,000 BBY as “The Old Republic.” People in the New Republic called the government of the prequel era “The Old Republic.” And “The Old Republic” is a video game and book series. Name: Ben Choucroun
Question: Who/What was Yuuzhan Vong?
Answer: Alright, so this will basically be a short crash course on the Vong for anyone wanting to learn about them. The Vong were a nihilistic alien race from outside the Star Wars Galaxy. After their own galaxy was devastated by wars, the Vong left their galaxy and traveled through the intergalactic void to the Star Wars Galaxy. After sending in various probes and spies, they invaded the galaxy in 25 ABY. The Vong were a warrior culture, and used completely organic technology. Everything, from their starships to battlecruisers to melee weapons, were living beings. The Vong (partly because of a devastating war between to droid races in their galaxy) were extremely technophobic. The Yuuzhan Vong traveled in massive living worldships, the largest of which, the Banuu Rass, was over 100km in length. At the end of each arm you can see a Miid Ro’ik class cruiser, a photo of which I’ll post in the comments. This can give you a good sense of how massive the things are. The Vong were very religious. They worshipped various gods, such as Yun-Yuuzhan (the creator) and Yun-Harla, the trickster god. The Vong would often make sacrifices to these gods, and even the idea that these gods might not exist was blashpemy. The Vong also had a very strict caste system. The Shamed Ones were at the bottom, and the Shaper and Warrior Castes at the top. The Shaper Caste not only helped grow the Vong’s living weapons, but also did body modifications, something the Vong were extremely fond of. So, that is what you need to know about the Yuuzhan Vong in Legends. In fact, the Yuuzhan Vong caused 365 trillion deaths and permanently messed up Jaina and Jacen Solo. I could go on an on about the Vong- about how they had a living planet called Zenoma Sekot and they had a torture device called the embrace of pain- but that’s ofr another day. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: If Lucas is so bad at dialogue, then how are Obi-Wan’s lines so hilarious and perfectly timed?
Answer: A couple things. First off, Lucas’ struggles with dialogue mainly come during the Original Trilogy. Mark Hammil even said that Lucas couldn’t write dialogue to save his life. But by the Prequel Trilogy his dialogue had greatly improved- in fact many of his lines were genius[1][2][3] I mean, the whole scene of Palpatine’s speech is so well written. From the actual speech itself to “So this is how liberty dies…” the scene is very well written. (On a side note, I love how it contrasts to Anakin killing the Separatist Council- the real damage is being done with words, not lightsabers). Plus, we have the Tragedy of Darth Plageuis the Wise, the dialogue between Anakin and Obi-Wan on Mustafar, I don’t like sand (a genius line), and the dialogue between Palpatine and Yoda. The prequel’s dialogue can be not just good, but exceptional at points. So, in conclusion, Lucas isn’t bad with dialogue. I won’t pretend the prequels had perfect dialogue- but they weren’t as bad as some would lead you to believe. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: What happened to Admiral Raddus and his crew after the event of Rogue One: A Star Wars Story?

Name: Ben Choucroun
Question: How did Mon Mothma have the authority to send the Rebel fleet to Scarif? The Rebel Council had already voted no. Why did she do so if she had already said no?
Answer: A couple reasons. First off, Mon Mothma had the absolute authority to send the Alliance to Scarif. The Alliance was an autocracy, with Mothma as its leader (something that Imperial propagandists delighted in pointing out). And although this position did have a built in expiration date, Mothma had the complete authority to do whatever she wanted with the Alliance military. People like Jan Doddona and Raddus were in her cabinet- for example, Doddona lead starfighter command, Raddus the fleet, and Nower Jebel was the minister of finance. As for why she sent the Alliance fleet, well, Admiral Raddus has disobeyed her orders and had left for Scarif in his ship. Mothma knew that Raddus was going to Scarif no matter what, and taking their largest capital ship with them. Mothma figured that she might as well support Raddus, so she sent the starfighters and smaller ships based at Yavin to assist Raddus, lest they lose the Profundity. She also knew that in the event of a large scale battle, the Raddus would need starfighters and support ships. So, that is why Mon Motha sent the Rebel fleet to Scarif. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: What's the worst job to have in Star Wars?

Name: Ben Choucroun
Question: What were all of the Rebel ships used during the Battle of Scarif?
Answer: All right, I’ll look at all the Rebel ships used during the Battle of Scarif. It’s quite possible that I’ll forget one, if I do, please let me know. X-Wings The Alliance used several squadrons of T-65 X-Wing starfighters at Scarif. An all around solid fighter, the X-Wing was superior to the TIE Fighter in almost every way. X-Wings took down the shields on the Star Destroyer Persecutor at Scarif. Y-Wings The Alliance also used Y-Wing starfighters. Powerful bombers, the Y-Wings were extremely useful despite being relics of the Clone Wars. Y-Wing bombers used ion torpedoes to disable the Star Destroyer Persecutor during the battle. U-Wing The Rebel Alliance deployed several U-Wings during the battle. The U-Wings were worth their weight in gold, as they were both a powerful transport and fighter. The U-Wings only downside was that they could only deploy 8 soldiers. VCX-100 A VCX-100 light freighter was also deployed at Scarif. Named the Ghost, it participated in battle at Scarif, Endor, and Exegol. It was also prominently featured in Rebels. GR-75 medium transport These ships were also deployed by the Alliance at Scarif. Mainly acting as transports, they could also be given turbolasers and sent to act as picket ships. However, being unarmored and ungainly made them easy pickings for TIE Fighters. Braha’tok Class Gunship Perhaps my favorite capital ship on this list, the Braha’tok class gunship was unique because it was the only rebel capital ship originally built for combat. Manufactured by Dornean Rebels, large quantities of these were shipped to the Alliance. The gunship first appeared in Return of the Jedi, where it was made by kit bashing. It since appeared in EU works until it found its way into Rogue One. The gunship works best when deployed in large numbers, and by getting up close and personal with the Star Destroyers, where it could unleash its powerful turbolasers. (And where it is harder for the ISD’s guns to target) Sphyrna-class corvette The Alliance also used several Sphyrna-class corvettes, nicknamed the Hammerhead Corvette. Used as a heavy attack craft, Hammerhead Corvettes could tangle with ships much larger than them as well as screen starfighters. CR-90 Corvette Nickaned the Rebel blockade runner, the Alliance used at least 6 CR-90 corvettes. The CR-90 was best used to scree starfighters, however, it’s powerful engines allowed it to land glancing shots on Star Destroyers before quickly leaving unscathed. Nebulon-B Frigate The backbone of the Rebel Fleet, the Nebulon B could serve many purposes. It was great against starfighters, having 12 laser cannons and 12 turbolasers. Several Nebulon Bs could , with support, sometimes challenge ISDs, although the Star Destroyer’s superior firepower usually allowed it to come out on top. MC-75 cruiser The MC-75 Profundity was the only Rebel ship that could really challenge an Imperial Star Destroyer. At over 1,000 meters in length, it was by far the largest ship in the Rebel arsenal. Admiral Raddus’ flagship, the Profundity, fought during the battle. So, those are the various rebel ships used during the Battle of Scarif. Stay safe, -Ben

Name: Ben Choucroun
Question: Why did Darth Vader kill Nute Gunray last while slaughtering the Separatist Leaders on Mustafar?
Answer: There are several reasons. First off, Sidious had no reason to keep Nute Gunray alive. Sidious used Gunray and the rest of the Separatist Council as pawns in his plans to take over the galaxy. Once Palpatine had successfully done so, he didn’t need Gunray, so he killed him. After all, Gunray was a loose end, and Palpatine wanted to kill Gunray so that no one would know that he was behind the Clone Wars. I mean, consider that Vader never killed Gunray, and he was instead captured an imprisoned. Perhaps a vengeful Gunray, facing a death sentence, might reveal clues that could lead people to learn of Darth Sidious’ true identity? Next up, Palpatine was afraid of any Separatist Remnants. It was a possibility that Gunray or another of the Separatist leaders could work to create a rebellion against the Empire, something Palpatine wanted to avoid. A Geonosian named Gizor Dellso survived in Legends and restarted the droid factories on Mustafar, creating a rebellion. Finally, it helped cement Anakin’s fall to the Dark Side. By having Anakin murder people in cold blood, (a reason why Palpatine had Anakin kill the younglings) Sidious further cemented Anakin’s allegiance to the Sith. So, that is why Palpatine had Anakin kill the Separatist Council. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: In Star Wars, why did people just accept the transition from the Galactic Republic to the Galactic Empire?
Answer: Often times, civilians accept absolute monarchs after a period of conflict. See, many times throughout history, people have accepted absolute rulers following a period of conflict. Off of the top of my head, Europeans accepted many absolute monarchs following the religious wars of the 17th century. The same applies to Star Wars. Many people, following the death and destruction of the Clone Wars, were happy to relinquish some freedoms in exchange for order and security. To quote The Essential Guide to Warfare, Padme Amidala called the Rise of the New Order the death of liberty, accompanied by thunderous applause. But on many war torn worlds, the applause was legitimate. So, that is why people were ok with the rise of the Empire. After the chaos of the Clone Wars, people wanted stability. Stay safe, -Ben

Question: In Star Wars, The super star destroyer is the largest ship in the Galaxy, with a crew of 280,000. What is the purpose of this ship? How would they feed the countless people aboard?
Answer: First off, the Super Star Destroyer is big. At 19 kilometers long, it was one of the largest ships in the galaxy. This means that it likely had plenty of room to store canned foods. According to The Official Star Wars Fact File, it had 6 years worth of consumables, so it only had to resupply rarely. Now, the Super Star Destroyer had two ways of resupplying. The first was ships bringing them food and fuel. A great example is the Altor-class replenishment ship, which is made up of massive containers of fuel and food. Next up, Super Star Destroyers often docked at orbital shipyards to resupply. The station Validusia was a great example, as it had room for at least 5 dreadnaughts to stop and resupply. As for why the Super Star Destroyer was built, there are two reasons. First off, when it was built, the Executor was the longest ship ever built. It was a massive symbol of fear. And second off, SSDs were great as mobile bases and command centers. Even the threat of an SSD could keep an entire sector in line. So, that is how the SSD was resupplied, and why they were made. Stay safe, -Ben

Name: Ben Choucroun
Question: In the space navies of Star Wars, why is the focus on large capital ships like the Imperial Star Destroyer rather than spacefighter carriers?
Answer: A couple things. First off, there are quite a bit of carriers in Star Wars. The Imperial-class Star Destroyer could carry a respectable 72 fighters. The Secutor, a dedicated carrier, could carry twice that amount. The Venator-class Star Destroyer could hold a whopping 420 starfighters. However, there is a reason why the Rebel Alliance never really used dedicated carriers in battle. (There are exceptions, in canon Phoenix Cell used a Quasar). That is because of their naval doctrine. See, the Alliance practiced space denial. Essentially, all Rebel starfighters had hyperdrives. This allowed the Alliance to jump in system, use their starfighters to quickly deal a load of damage, and then leave before the enemy could launch their TIE Fighters. Having a carrier makes that useless. The Alliance would have to deploy and then recall their fighters, which takes time. Their whole naval doctrine is based around the idea that they don’t actually need carriers. So why use carriers? I’d like to briefly touch on the other factions as well. The Imperial-class Star Destroyer could carry 72 TIEs, as I mentioned earlier. I also touched on the carrying capacity of the Venator, but the Lucrehulk could carry 1,500 droid fighters. So, in conclusion, with the exception of the Rebel Alliance, carriers are used a lot. Plus, lots of famous capital ships can carry a lot of starfighters. Stay safe, -Ben
